reason: E2 confirms Nb forms Ni3Nb in Ni-base superalloys and that refractory elements improve properties in Ti and Ni alloys, supporting the first two premises. The precipitation hardening mechanism is textbook knowledge. However, no cited evidence addresses whether a Ti-Ni-primary HEA can be single-phase or whether Nb addition will produce fine, uniform precipitates in that specific matrix; these premises are unsupported.
premises: Nb forms Ni3Nb γ″ phase in Ni-base superalloys
Refractory elements improve mechanical properties in Ti and Ni alloys
Precipitation of fine intermetallics hinders dislocations and improves high-temperature strength
A Ti-Ni-primary HEA can be made single-phase solid solution without Nb
Adding ~5 at% Nb to such an HEA will form fine, uniformly distributed Nb-rich precipitates
